$Comment: 2026-10-22 sounds (SFX_AT_Ice_King_* events, rule: each sound on its exact moment): VO_Phase4_Growl with the PhaseChange and VO_Scream_Long 1.7 s later; VO_Shield_Break on the shield's 5th hit (1); VO_Low_Health once under 15 % health and VO_Low_Health_Laugh every 25 s while under it. 2026-10-22 balance (picked after an art review, ice-king-balance-review.md): timers Zap 6, RayBoth 7, Freeze 10, Burst_Single 20, Burst 24 s (were 3/4/6/12/16; they asked for about 185 % of his time, so most were lost); shield off; summons only while 0-5 Gunters are around (was 0-9). 2026-10-22 (playtest: phase 4 should be the hardest; he mostly flew and used the basic ray, a special only now and then; more cadence): timers Zap 4, RayBoth 5, Freeze 7, Burst_Single 12, Burst 15, Ultimate 30, Rain 18 s (were 6/7/10/20/24/40/25); every timed attack also waits while he is casting (Not Self IsExecutingInteraction), so when its timer is up it fires as soon as he is free instead of being lost. 2026-10-22: every Attack action has DamageFriendlies true. The henchmen list the king's group in DisableDamageGroups (so they never fight back at him); with this flag his attacks still land on them as before (ultimate, stray rays), while their Damage sensor still ignores him. 2026-10-22 (harness fight, attack counts per phase): the attack timers are no longer Repeating. A repeating timer restarts by itself at 0, so its rule (Timer TimeRemainingRange [0, 1] + Not IsExecutingInteraction) could only fire during the last second of each cycle; when the king was busy then (Zap and Ray_Both kept him busy most of the time) that attack was skipped for a whole cycle: phase 2 cast Sword_Dive 0 times in 3 min, phase 4 the ultimate once. A non-repeating timer stops at 0 (Timer.tick) and waits there, the rule fires as soon as he is free, and the rule's TimerRestart starts the next cycle. When several are ready, the first rule in file order goes first, so Zap (near the end) fills the gaps instead of starving the rest. 2026-10-22 (playtest: switch off friendly-fire avoidance on all his attacks; if he kills his own penguins by mistake, better, a more chaotic team fight): every Attack action has AvoidFriendlyFire false (ActionAttack: with true, an entity of his own damage groups in the line made him drop the attack). 2026-10-22 (playtest: phase 4 only spawned Gunters, no snowmen): the air summon now spawns snowmen too (gunters 3->2, +2 snowmen; count group -> AT_Ice_King_Minions), like the ground summon (Projectile_Config_AT_Ice_King_Summon: Gunters + a snowman); its limit counts both (group AT_Ice_King_Minions, was Gunters only). 2026-10-22: phase 4 spawns AT_Gunter_Minion_Enraged / AT_Snowman_Minion_Enraged (50 % Ice resistance, AT_Ice_King_Ice_Body_Half), so his ice hurts them; phases 1-3 keep the 100 % henchmen.

Content.$Comment: Phase 4 (AT_Ice_King_Air_Enraged) extra combat behaviour, plugged into the vanilla Template_Flying_Aggressive hook CombatAdditionalBehaviorComponent; it runs before the template's own ranged attack (the normal ice ray). A flying template has no CAE, so the extra attacks go on timers here. 1) Health regen off once. 2) Freezing ray every 6 s (first after 3 s) when the target is within 24 blocks in sight: And(Target, Timer) + HeadMotion Aim + Attack, the pattern of vanilla Template_Dungeon_Goblin_Lobber's enraged lane. The Attack action starts nothing while another attack runs, so it never overlaps the normal ray. 3) Every 15 s (first after 6 s), while at most 9 Gunters are within 30 blocks, summon 3 (12 at most); same pattern as Component_AT_Ice_King_Air_Combat. 2026-10-21: circles around the player (AT_CIRCLE, radius 13) instead of hovering over his head. 2026-10-21 (playtest: harder in the rage phase): every HeadMotion Aim here has Deflection true, so he aims where the player WILL be (HeadMotionAim: target velocity in the ballistic solution). It only works for attacks with an AimingReference projectile (the ice ray, the freezing ray); bolts without one (Zap, burst) and the beam still aim at where the player is.

Instructions.$Comment: 2026-10-21: phase-change animation (AT_Ice_King model set PhaseChange, Status slot) once when he reaches combat in this role. The flying template's Alerted state plays a fixed Alerted animation, so the air roles shorten AlertedTime and this one plays right after it. 2026-10-22 (playtest: in phase 2 the laugh played many times a second): an 'Any, Once' sensor here re-arms every time the combat component is entered again, which the flying template does often, so the phase line (and the PhaseChange animation) repeated nonstop. Now guarded by the flag AT_Ice_King_Phase4_Voice: it runs while the flag is not set and sets it, so it plays once per role.

2026-10-22 (playtest: the Gunters and snowmen defend the king like a pack, whoever attacks him, they go after them): on every tick he takes combat damage, store the attacker (Damage sensor TargetSlot, as vanilla Component_Instruction_Void_Anomaly_Death's LastAttacker) and send it as the payload of a 'Flock_Attack' beacon (SendTargetSlot) to the AT_Ice_King_Minions group within 40 blocks. Template_Predator (the henchmen's base) already listens for 'Flock_Attack' while Idle or asleep (TargetSlot LockedTarget, then Combat.Maybe / Alerted) once its FlockArray is set, which the henchmen roles now do. A Beacon to a group, not a flock: flock members cannot hurt each other and an attacker holds fire when a flock friend is in its line (PositionCache.isFriendlyBlockingLineOfSight), so he stays out of their flock.

2026-10-22 multiplayer (like the Gobliterator spreading its attacks): when hit, the air attacks switch to whoever did the most damage (Damage sensor TargetSlot LockedTarget = DamageData.getMostDamagingAttacker), at most every 6 s (timer first in the And: SensorAnd stops at the first false, so the Damage sensor only rebinds when the timer is done).

2026-10-22 multiplayer: every 8-12 s without a damage switch, lock onto the nearest OTHER player within 60 blocks (Player sensor IgnoredTargetSlot LockedTarget + LockOnTarget), so the air phases do not chase one player all fight. Alone, no other player matches and nothing changes.

2026-10-22 VO_Many_Players (approximation, no sensor tells who hit him): he is hit while 2 or more players are within 24 blocks (Count with IncludeGroups Player, SensorCount.groupListHasPlayer), at most every 90 s (timer AT_Ice_King_ManyPlayers, first possible 5 s into the role).

2026-10-22: VO_Low_Health ('Please!') once when his health drops under 15 % (Self + Stat filter, as vanilla Component_Feran_Sensor_Low_HP). Only phase 4 gets that low: the encounter changes phase at higher health. 2026-10-22 (playtest: phase 2 and 4 voices looped nonstop): 'Any, Once' re-arms every time the flying template re-enters this combat component (it flips between combat and chase whenever line of sight flickers), so it is replaced by a flag set the first time: once per role.
2026-10-22: under 15 % health, the nervous laugh VO_Low_Health_Laugh now and then: timer AT_Ice_King_Air_Enraged_Laugh (first after 12 s, then every 25 s).

Ice shield hit counter (2026-10-21: the shield breaks after 5 s or 5 hits): a hit taken while AT_Ice_King_Ice_Shield is on moves the invisible counter up one step (Damage sensor: true only on the tick he took damage, NPCEntity.clearDamageData every tick; hits from his own group do not count). Highest step first, so one hit moves exactly one step. 5th hit: AT_Ice_King_Shield_Broken, and AT_Ice_King_Ice_Shield bursts. Continue, nothing else is stopped.

AT_CIRCLE 1/2: move the leash point onto the target every tick (target within 60 blocks; 40 until 2026-10-21, past it the leash point stayed behind and the soft leash pulled him away) (SetLeashPosition ToTarget), so WanderInCircle below circles around the player, not around where the king spawned (BodyMotionWanderInCircle.getReferencePoint = NPCEntity.getLeashPoint).

2026-10-22 (playtest: the rage ultimate beam turned so fast it was almost impossible to dodge): while AT_Ice_King_Beam_Focus_Rage is on him (the rage beam's charge and fire), turn the body with the head (MatchLook) but aim slowly: HeadMotion Aim RelativeTurnSpeed 0.25 and no lead (Deflection false), so the sweep follows the player at a quarter of the normal turn speed. Placed before the casting MatchLook rule: the first body/head motion of a tick wins. 2026-10-22 (running sideways: the rage beam still caught up too fast): RelativeTurnSpeed 0.12 (was 0.25), half the sweep speed. Then 0.175 (after trying 0.12).

2026-10-21 (playtest: the ray still went where he was not): while he casts, turn the body toward the target. The circle already stops during a cast, but the template Seek that took over does nothing inside CombatSeekStopDistance, and a flier then keeps flying straight (MotionControllerFly, MinAirSpeed), so the head (Camera yaw +-60 from the body) still could not reach the player. MatchLook sets the body yaw to the head yaw every tick (BodyMotionMatchLook), so the body chases the aiming head until it faces the player; the first body motion of the tick wins, so it beats the Seek. Flight turn 180 deg/s, the ray leaves 0.8 s into the cast.

AT_ORBIT (2026-10-22: he hovered right over his head, he had to aim almost straight up; 40-50 degrees wanted). Replaces the WanderInCircle (radius 17), which picks random points INSIDE the circle and so crossed over the player; an AT_RING Flee tried the same day made him fly at ground level and was removed. Now 8 waypoints on a ring of radius 13 around the player, 13 blocks above him, so about 45 degrees up (horizontal distance = height). Each is the target's position plus an offset (AdjustPosition wrapping the Target sensor, as vanilla Template_Goblin_Scrapper wraps ReadPosition; the And sensor takes the first position, SensorAnd), flown to with the same Seek as the template's combat Seek (DesiredAltitudeWeight 1). The repeating timer AT_Ice_King_Air_Enraged_Orbit (16 s) picks one waypoint per 2 s in order, so he goes round the player. Not while he casts (MatchLook turns him toward the player then). The template's OverrideAltitude (10-15 over the ground) still runs. Continue, so the timers below still run. Tune: radius and height in each Offset, seconds per waypoint in the TimeRemainingRange slices. 2026-10-22 (log: the waypoint rules were active the whole time but he did not move toward them): Seek UsePathfinder false and SkipSteering false. BodyMotionFind skips steering when its probe says the goal is not reached in a straight line (shouldSkipSteering), then falls back to the pathfinder, which waits 3-5 s after a failed search (ThrottleDelayRange); the waypoint changes every 2-3 s, so he never got going. In open air pure steering is enough. 2026-10-22, later (playtest: now he gets stuck in trees): pure steering flies straight into canopies, so the pathfinder is back as a fallback (UsePathfinder true) while steering is still tried first (SkipSteering false), and a failed path search waits 0.5-1 s instead of 3-5 (ThrottleDelayRange).
